newsitem.title: USA: United States to gather evidence in Saudi case.
newsitem.headline: United States to gather evidence in Saudi case.

text.p: The United States will gather evidence overseas against a Saudi dissident who pulled out of a deal to provide information about a 1996 bombing in Saudi Arabia, Attorney General Janet Reno said on Thursday.
The dissident, Hani al-Sayegh, was indicted for conspiring during 1994 and 1995 to kill Americans residing in Saudi Arabia, charges unrelated to the 1996 truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen.

Sayegh on Wednesday backed out of an earlier plea agreement in which he was to plead guilty to the conspiracy charge and cooperate with the U.S. investigation of the bombing. He instead pleaded innocent.
"The U.S. will now focus its attention on obtaining from overseas the necessary witnesses and the evidence to proceed to trial in this case," Reno said at her weekly Justice Department news briefing.
"Additionally, we continue to pursue aggressively all avenues of investigation relating" to the bombing, Reno said.
She declined comment on whether deporting Sayegh to Saudi Arabia was an option. Sayegh's lawyer has said he fears execution if returned to his homeland.

Sayegh's repudiation of the plea deal represented a major embarrassment for the U.S. government, which arranged his deportation from Canada in June and hoped he might provide valuable information about those responsible for the bombing.
Reno denied FBI agents and Justice Department officials who arranged for Sayegh's deportation, questioned him in Canada and reached the plea deal, had bungled the case.
"No, that was carefully reviewed," she said. "Everybody worked together on that. And I don't find that they did anything that was inappropriate. In fact, their work has been excellent," she said.
